note: Fee-on-transfer token, and the most dangerous of the three on this chain because it is taxed in BOTH directions at DIFFERENT rates: 400 bps on transfers INTO its USDC pool 0x183fff18ccbdda0b5aa1c9d9ddeef00d3803b8c0 (the cited transaction) and 100 bps on transfers OUT of it (measured by debug_traceCall at head against the same pool). feeBps carries the higher, conservative 400. That pool is NOT a Uniswap V3 pool -- its factory is 0x942Bd5BFdc5317C5507e326f8EB4BB6058AB5C10 and it exposes neither fee() nor tickSpacing() -- which is why it does not appear in vfat-db's uniswap_v3_pools and why ARCADE deliberately has NO curated per-pool tax row: a rate cannot be keyed against a venue the indexer does not carry. Blocklisting is therefore the ONLY protection for this token today. Its taxed transfers were found while sweeping for the signature; the venue was identified afterwards from the transfer's recipient.

note: Fee-on-transfer token: a taxed transfer emits TWO Transfer events with the SAME sender -- 99% to the intended recipient and 1% credited to the token contract itself. Both legs are in the receipt, so the split is reproducible from eth_getLogs alone with no tracing. The tax is POOL-SCOPED, not token-wide: transfers out of the USDC fee-10000 pool 0x6a3bacaa6493734c1ac221ebf42cf530a96c1e02 are taxed, while ordinary holder-to-holder transfers and transfers out of every other ARGUS pool probed (USDC at fee 0/100/500/3000, a second USDC fee-10000 pool on a different factory, SMKA, TEST, TOLLY) are NOT. Smaller populations at other rates appear when replaying logs (sub-1 bps residues from unrelated transfers); feeBps carries the dominant rate the cited pool exhibits. This token caused a live incident: vfat-router quoted the pool's GROSS output while SwapRouter received 99%, so /v4/zap-in returned 400 InsufficientOutputAmount for any user at 0.5% slippage -- intermittently, because it cleared whenever price drifted the user's way by more than their slippage. Failure modes by position in a router path: (1) as INPUT or INTERMEDIATE on a constant-product venue -- the destination pool is credited only 99% of amountSent, so pool.swap reverts K(); (2) as TERMINAL OUTPUT -- the user receives 99% of the quoted amountOut, violating the minAmountOut promise. On a concentrated-liquidity venue the pool is paid in full and the PAYER is surcharged instead, so the sell leg is a silent extra cost rather than a revert.
